channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Tencent Cloud Chief Says AI Demand Justifies Capex
item.description: Dowson Tong, CEO of Tencent Cloud and Smart Industries Group in an exclusive conversation with BTV's Stephen Engle talks about the company's investment shifts from being AI consumer agents to enterprise, why it is prioritizing compute for internal model training and products and the competition on chatbot space. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Samsung Electronics Shares Slide After Return Plan Is Delayed
item.description: Samsung Electronics Co. shares reversed earlier gains to slide as much as 6.6% as the lack of a new shareholder return plan in its earnings disappointed investors.
item.dc:creator: Winnie Hsu and Youkyung Lee

item.title: Samsung Chip Operating Profit Misses Estimates
item.description: Samsung reported net for the third quarter that missed the average analyst estimate. Bloomberg's Haidi Stroud-Watts breaks down the numbers. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Samsung Boosts Spending After Chip Profit Misses Estimates
item.description: Samsung Electronics Co. hiked its spending plans after relentless demand for AI infrastructure drove memory prices higher, though its chip division’s profit missed lofty investor expectations.
item.dc:creator: Yoolim Lee

item.title: Nscale’s Unproven CEO Braves AI Turmoil in Bid for $30 Billion Neocloud IPO
item.description: Sheryl Sandberg says the 32-year-old executive reminds her of Mark Zuckerberg. Josh Payne must now take his startup public at a tumultuous moment for the AI industry.
item.dc:creator: Mark Bergen

item.title: Equinix Says Data-Project Barriers Could Boost Its Pricing Power
item.description: Equinix Inc., one of the world’s biggest data-center companies, said mounting barriers to bringing new projects online will make existing capacity more valuable and potentially strengthen its grip on the market — including pricing.
item.dc:creator: Dina Katgara

item.title: Alphabet Shares Tank on Sales Misses Across Core Businesses
item.description: Alphabet posted disappointing sales from most of its core businesses in the third quarter, escalating investors’ concerns about the hundreds of billions of dollars that the company is spending on artificial intelligence. Ed Ludlow has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: FuriosaAI Quadruples Valuation to $2.9 Billion in Nvidia Chase
item.description: South Korean AI chip startup FuriosaAI quadrupled its valuation to $2.9 billion in a fresh funding round, bolstering its bid to challenge the likes of Nvidia Corp.
item.dc:creator: Yoolim Lee

item.title: Japan Credit Risk Jumps Most Since 2022, Pressuring Bond Market
item.description: A deterioration in global credit markets is showing up in Japan, where corporate credit risk has worsened by the most since September 2022, adding pressure to a bond market already absorbing record issuance.
item.dc:creator: Takahiko Hyuga

item.title: Schwab Says AI Making Scams Harder to Spot
item.description: Artificial intelligence is making financial scams more convincing and harder to detect, raising new risks for investors and financial advisors. Cayla Culver, Head of Risk and Controls for Schwab Advisor Services, says fraudsters are using AI to scale traditional scams and even spoof the voices of family members. She joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss how advisors can protect clients and their firms, and why Schwab is pushing for a consistent federal framework for cybersecurity incidents. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fed Holds Rates With a Hawkish Edge
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are DWS Americas CEO Hepsen Uzcan, Stony Brook University Public Policy & Economics Professor Stephanie Kelton, VF Corp CEO Bracken Darrell, Jersey Mike’s CEO Charlie Morrison, DoubleLine Capital Portfolio Manager Ken Shinoda, DA Davidson Managing Director, Head of Tech Research Gil Luria, Ford CFO Sherry House, Rosenblatt Securities Managing Director, Senior Research Analyst Scott Devitt, & Allspring Global Investments Senior Portfolio Analyst Abby Roach. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Banks Shelve Bond Sale for Anthropic-Tied Texas Data Center
item.description: Banks are delaying plans to offload part of a $15 billion loan to fund a data center tied to Anthropic PBC in Texas, after the state put a hold on new projects while assessing risks to its power grid.
item.dc:creator: Davide Barbuscia, Michelle Cheng and Gowri Gurumurthy

item.title: Charles Schwab Integrating AI Tools and Financial Planning
item.description: Charles Schwab is expanding its push into artificial intelligence, bringing Anthropic’s Claude for Financial Advisors directly into Schwab Advisor Center. The company says it is the first RIA custodian to offer Anthropic’s advisor-specific AI to independent firms. Alison Dooher, Head of AI at Schwab Advisor Services, joins Bloomberg Businessweek Live from Schwab IMPACT Summit in Boston to discuss how AI is changing the financial advice landscape. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Microsoft's Big Bets on AI Start to Pay Off
item.description: Microsoft Corp. reported better-than-expected cloud revenue, suggesting the company continues to reap the benefits of its massive investment in artificial intelligence. Sales at Azure were up 48%. Revenue from a commercial deal with OpenAI totaled $10 billion. Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow and Anurag Rana of Bloomberg Intelligence report. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Breaking Down Alphabet's Disappointing Earnings Report
item.description: Alphabet quarterly sales and profit missed estimates, with investors focused on whether the company can protect its search business as AI changes how people find information. Scott Devitt, managing director and senior research analyst at Rosenblatt Securities, breaks down Alphabet's earnings report on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Marvell Is Said to Near Megadeal for Lumentum In AI Push
item.description: Marvell Technology Inc. is in advanced talks to buy data center optics maker Lumentum Holdings Inc., according to people familiar with the matter, a potential megadeal amid the race to scale up in the artificial intelligence sector.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Gould, Michelle F. Davis and David Carnevali

item.title: Microsoft’s Surging Cloud Sales Show AI Spending Paying Off
item.description: Microsoft Corp. posted increasing growth in its cloud business and kept its capital expenditures in check, satisfying investors amid a drumbeat of concern that spending on artificial intelligence won’t pay off.
item.dc:creator: Brody Ford and Matt Day

item.title: Alphabet’s Revenue Miss Reignites Fears Over AI Spending Binge
item.description: Alphabet Inc.’s search and advertising sales disappointed in the most recent quarter, reinforcing investors’ fears that Google is losing ground to AI rivals despite pouring hundreds of billions of dollars into the technology.
item.dc:creator: Julia Love and Davey Alba

item.title: T-Mobile Boosts Profit, Adds Customers on New Rate Plans
item.description: T-Mobile US Inc. added more total customer accounts in the third quarter than analysts had expected, showing its slate of offers and loyalty incentives are resonating with customers.
item.dc:creator: Kelcee Griffis

item.title: Palantir’s Defense Chief Sees China Threat to Taiwan Over AI
item.description: Palantir Technologies Inc.’s head of defense Mike Gallagher is warning that advances in artificial intelligence capabilities have made it more compelling for Chinese leader Xi Jinping to seize control of Taiwan, a chipmaking hub that has helped fuel the global AI boom.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Eastland
